title: They crossed a line most people won’t even name.
paragraphs: They crossed a line most people won’t even name.
And the Bible didn’t hide it.

Lot’s daughters got their father drunk… and slept with him.
Not once.
Twice.
Silence.

So what is it?
Desperation… or depravity?
Here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

They had just escaped fire.
Sodom was ash.
Their mother—gone, turned to salt.
Their world? Erased in a single night.

No men.
No future.
No legacy.
Just fear echoing in a cave.
And then a decision.
“Let’s preserve our family line.”
That’s what they said.
But here’s what we miss…
Good intentions don’t cleanse sinful actions.

Yes, they were desperate.
But desperation doesn’t make sin righteous.

They chose deception.
They chose intoxication.
They chose incest.
And Scripture doesn’t soften it.

Their sons—Moab and Ben-Ammi—became nations marked by conflict with Israel.
Pain multiplied.
Consequences echoed.
Sin always echoes.
Even when it starts in fear.
But don’t miss this.
God didn’t erase them from the story.

Because the Bible isn’t a museum of perfect people.
It’s a rescue mission for broken ones.
Fast forward.

Generations later…
From Moab—yes, that line—comes a woman named Ruth.
Outcast. Widow. Foreigner.
Yet God writes her into redemption.
She becomes part of the lineage of Jesus Christ.
Let that hit you.
God can take the aftermath of scandal… and still write salvation through it.

Not because the sin was small.
But because His grace is bigger.
So what’s the verdict?

Desperation?
Yes.

Depravity?
Also yes.
That’s the human condition.
And that’s why we need a Savior.
Because left to ourselves, even our “survival instincts” can lead us into darkness.
But in Christ—

There is forgiveness.
There is cleansing.
There is a new story.
You are not trapped in the cave of your worst decision.
Jesus walks into caves.
And He brings light.

If this stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
Bring it to Him.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
